skill.name: relight
skill.description: Relight still images with RunComfy by changing lighting direction, color temperature, intensity, and mood while preserving subject identity and framing.
skill.summary: Relight still images through RunComfy using Qwen Edit Relight and related image-edit endpoints.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The static findings are dominated by Markdown backticks, documentation links, and stated RunComfy CLI usage rather than executable malicious code. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or hidden command behavior was found in SKILL.md; users should still understand that relighting sends approved image inputs to RunComfy and uses a local CLI token.

remediation.issue: External image processing service is required.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the privacy disclosure prominent and tell agents to confirm before sending private images or URLs to RunComfy.

remediation.issue: CLI token persists on disk after login.
remediation.suggestion: Continue documenting the token path, file mode, and CI environment variable option so users can manage credentials intentionally.

remediation.issue: Global CLI installation can affect the user environment.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer npx or documented package-manager installation and keep the warning against remote shell installers.

content.value_statement: Changing image lighting usually requires a new shoot or manual editing. This skill helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code route still-image relighting requests through RunComfy models.
actual_capabilities: Routes still-image relighting prompts to Qwen Edit 2509 Relight LoRA by default.
Suggests fallback RunComfy edit models for composite edits and reference-based lighting.
Provides command examples for running relight jobs with the runcomfy CLI.
Helps describe lighting direction, temperature, intensity, and mood in prompts.
Documents output handling through the CLI output directory.
limitations: Requires the runcomfy CLI and a valid RunComfy account or token.
Sends source images or image URLs to RunComfy model endpoints.
Targets still images, not video relighting workflows.
Lighting fidelity depends on the selected model and prompt clarity.

use_cases.title: Refresh catalog product lighting
use_cases.description: Convert plain product shots into warmer studio or lifestyle lighting while keeping orientation and color identity stable.

use_cases.title: Shift portrait mood
use_cases.description: Change portraits from flat or overcast lighting to golden hour, window light, or dramatic rim lighting.

use_cases.title: Prototype lighting directions
use_cases.description: Test several lighting styles before choosing a final look for campaigns or visual concepts.

prompt_templates.title: Basic relight
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Relight this image with warm golden hour lighting. Preserve the subject, pose, framing, and main colors.

prompt_templates.title: Product studio lighting
prompt_templates.scenario: Catalog image with controlled lighting direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Relight this product photo with a soft key light from camera-left, a weak fill from camera-right, and neutral 5500K color temperature. Preserve product shape and color.

prompt_templates.title: Portrait mood change
prompt_templates.scenario: Portrait edit with stronger mood control.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use RunComfy to relight this portrait as blue hour. Add a soft cool key light from the left and a subtle warm rim light from behind. Preserve identity and facial expression.

prompt_templates.title: Reference-style lighting match
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using a lighting reference.
prompt_templates.prompt: Match the lighting direction, contrast, and color temperature of the reference image while preserving the subject and composition of the source image.

output_examples.input: Relight a product image as warm window light from camera-left.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects the dedicated relight route, prepares a RunComfy command, and saves the edited image to the requested output folder.

output_examples.input: Make this portrait look like golden hour without changing the person.
output_examples.output: The assistant builds a preservation-focused prompt that specifies warm key light, rim light, and identity preservation.

output_examples.input: Apply the lighting style from this reference photo to my source image.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a reference-capable edit route and describes how to preserve the source subject while matching lighting.

best_practices: State the light source, direction, color temperature, and intensity in the same prompt.
Always ask to preserve subject identity, framing, pose, and important colors.
Use user-provided image URLs only, and confirm that the images may be sent to RunComfy.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for unrelated object edits when lighting is not the main change.
Do not pass private image URLs unless the user has approved external processing.
Do not install the CLI from unverified scripts or pipe remote installers into a shell.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images from text only?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on relighting existing still images. Use a text-to-image skill for new image generation.

faq.question: Which model does it use first?
faq.answer: It defaults to Qwen Edit 2509 Relight LoRA for dedicated lighting changes.

faq.question: Can it match lighting from a reference image?
faq.answer: Yes, the skill recommends reference-capable edit routes when the task needs a source image and a lighting reference.

faq.question: Does it work for video?
faq.answer: No. The documented CLI flow is for still images. Video relighting requires separate RunComfy workflows.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the RunComfy CLI and sends jobs to RunComfy model endpoints.

faq.question: How should I protect private images?
faq.answer: Use only approved image URLs or local assets, and confirm that external processing is acceptable before running the command.
